headline: Town boards finalized recommendations and warrant articles for Special Town Meeting, focusing on water connections, zoning, and open space funding requests.
synopsis: Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Advisory Committee completed its report, voting 6-0 to recommend approval of a $240,000 water connection near Parkerville Road while finalizing unfavorable positions on funding for a trail footbridge and golf course irrigation. The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the Peninsula Trail bridge funding article to town meeting as written, and the Trails Committee decided against offering a floor amendment to cut project contingency. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to advance a warrant article permitting two-family dwellings as drafted, despite concerns about lot requirements. Additionally, regional school subcommittees reviewed FY28 budget planning, highlighting an upcoming $800,000 net decrease in high school debt service.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail bridge funding moves to Town Meeting as drafted
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to present the $217,318 CPA funding request as printed, and the Trails Committee dropped a potential floor amendment to cut project contingency.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee recommends Parkerville Road water main extension
highlights.why: The committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approve $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the landfill to municipal water, with the town covering lines into the homes.

highlights.title: Zoning Board supports two-family dwelling warrant article
highlights.why: Members voted unanimously to advance the proposed zoning amendment as written rather than make last-minute revisions concerning minimum lot sizes in business and residential districts.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee report opposes CPA funding for golf and trail bridge
highlights.why: In finalizing its warrant report, the committee maintained opposition to spending CPA funds on the $1 million golf course irrigation project and $428,550 trail bridge, citing excessive costs and golf self-sufficiency.

highlights.title: Regional high school debt drop and FY28 capital requests presented
highlights.why: Subcommittees reviewed $460,000 in proposed FY28 capital work and noted that expiring 2004 renovation bonds will lower regional debt service by about $800,000 across both towns.
highlights.body: Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee Operational Budget and Capital Planning Subcommittees
